Once the inherent unity of the essential self is recognized, the psyche is relieved of the burden of feigning unity. It can admit itself it's own composite nature, and accept the hidden realms of its dream and shadow. This thus allows the psyche to perform a taxonomy of its own elements, without fear of utter disintegration. It can then begin the process of unification, whereby conflicts existing on the mental, somatic and soulical levels, or which are expressed between or across these levels, can be rectified. Then unity becomes a question not of an intrapsychic nature, which the psyche cannot unambiguously claim, but one of the oneness of Being, which alone can, and Indeed must, affirm unity. For Psyche, it becomes a question of harmonization, reconciliation and cooperation, grounded in the unity of Being, which for Psyche is its identity with God.
